memos.risk:
Risk officer call: refuse any size.

Key facts: the coin is down 84% from its 30-minute high and 70% in the last 15 minutes, with net outflow and sells nearly matching buys. Pool depth is only 82.9 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip, and a stop of 20-50% in a thin, collapsing pool, risks slippage well past the stop. The 36% bundle share and launch bot suggest coordinated activity, and the metadata host is unverified, which we treat as data only. Momentum is broken and the base rate for buying a falling coin in this window is poor. Skip it. Revisit only if the pool deepens materially and price stabilizes for several intervals with net buy flow.
memos.scout:
There is no honest case for buying PUTER now. The brief shows a coin already down 84% from its 30-minute high, with a 70% loss over the last 15 minutes and net outflow of 50 SOL in that window. Sellers (1,304) outnumber buyers (1,260) and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.93, so the early buyers are exiting rather than holding.

The only constructive reading is that the 502 buyers and roughly $179k of recent volume show there is still interest, and the curve data is not dominated by a single actor (top-3 share 7%, top-5 buyer share 12%). But that is a description of past activity, not evidence that demand will still be here in 30-60 minutes. A coin in a steep, sustained drawdown with heavy net selling sits well below the base rate of about -20% per trade for alive coins, and a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs on top of that. The desk should skip.
